scenario: Analysts need a churn baseline over BigQuery tables, can work in SQL, and need minimal infrastructure.
decision: Start with BigQuery ML and define when a managed or custom Vertex AI path becomes justified.
must_evidence: unsupported-model or control threshold for migration
trap: Choosing custom distributed training because it appears more sophisticated.

scenario: A document assistant must answer from company material with citations and changing permissions.
decision: Choose a grounded managed architecture and its evaluation boundaries.
trap: Fine-tuning the model to memorize changing private documents.

scenario: A team needs OCR and entity extraction but owns little labeled data and no ML operations team.
decision: Compare pretrained API, AutoML, and custom model options.
trap: Defaulting to custom training before benchmarking managed APIs.

scenario: Offline features score well, but online predictions differ because event-time joins leak future information.
trap: Retraining without correcting leakage and skew.

scenario: Several researchers share a notebook environment containing sensitive training data.
trap: Sharing one powerful service account for convenience.

scenario: A promising experiment cannot be reproduced after its author leaves.
trap: Preserving only the final model file.

scenario: A tabular problem has limited data and strict explanation requirements; a deep network was proposed by default.
decision: Select and baseline model families based on constraints.
trap: Assuming greater model complexity guarantees better business performance.

scenario: Training takes days on CPU, but profiling shows input starvation rather than dense compute saturation.
decision: Choose the next optimization before buying accelerators.
trap: Adding GPUs without fixing the data bottleneck.

scenario: A hyperparameter sweep consumes budget while trials repeat weak regions.
trap: Maximizing trial count without an explicit resource budget.

scenario: Millions of overnight records tolerate six-hour latency and do not need per-request responses.
decision: Choose batch prediction and justify it against an online endpoint.
trap: Paying for continuously available online serving.

scenario: Interactive traffic has unpredictable bursts and sensitive payloads.
decision: Design endpoint exposure and scaling controls.
trap: Treating private networking as a replacement for authorization.

scenario: A candidate model has better aggregate accuracy but worse results for one high-impact segment.
trap: Promoting solely on the aggregate metric.

scenario: A pipeline trains successfully on malformed data and registers a poor model.
decision: Place conditional gates throughout the pipeline.
trap: Using job completion as the model-quality gate.

scenario: Feature drift crosses a threshold, but labels arrive weeks later.
trap: Automatically replacing production whenever input drift fires.

scenario: Training and serving use separate preprocessing code that has begun to diverge.
trap: Monitoring output drift without repairing transformation ownership.

scenario: Input distributions are stable while prediction accuracy declines as customer behavior changes.
decision: Classify and respond to the change.
must_evidence: concept drift distinguished from data drift
trap: Concluding no drift exists because feature distributions are stable.

scenario: A public generative endpoint accepts prompts that try to exfiltrate hidden instructions and retrieved secrets.
must_evidence: input/output inspection or Model Armor role

scenario: Overall model quality is stable, but explanation attributions and refusal rates shift for one language.
decision: Extend continuous monitoring and release controls.
trap: Using a global average that hides slice regressions.
